The notebook

The notebook was small enough to carry in a coat pocket. By November, its corners had softened and the cover had begun to remember the shape of a hand.

Most pages held ordinary things: the name of a book, a sentence overheard on the train, the hours of a shop she kept arriving at after it had closed.

A note for the next draft

Keep the opening concrete. Let the change in the room carry the ending.
